question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=-8,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=6,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=0$ are eigenvalues, and 

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-8,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=6,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=0,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-8,$

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=6,$ and

- the $3$rd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{3}=0.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -3 & -6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
